papers.title: $L^1$ stability of the entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$ without moment assumptions
papers.abstract: We establish qualitative stability in $L^1$ and Ruzsa distance for Shannon's entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$, without any moment assumptions. The proof uses the optimal transport argument by Rioul (2017), majorization bounds of density rearrangements, and the stability of the sharp form of Young's inequality due to Christ (2019). Along the way we also extend recent one-dimensional results on de Bruijn's identity, the continuity of differential entropy, and the equality case of the entropy power inequality to random vectors of any dimension.

papers.title: On the convergence of greedy algorithms in one-dimensional Wasserstein space
papers.abstract: We study the convergence of the greedy algorithm for approximating a compact set by barycenters in metric spaces, in particular in the space of one-dimensional measures endowed with the 2-Wasserstein distance. To this end, we compare several metric $N$-widths, which measure the best error achievable with $N$-point barycenters, using either classical barycenters having nonnegative weights or signed barycenters, with weights of arbitrary sign summing to one. For the analysis we exploit that quantile functions embed the one-dimensional 2-Wasserstein space isometrically into a convex cone of $L^2(0,1)$, and barycenter sets correspond to nonlinear projections of convex or affine hulls. We prove, both in the algebraic and exponential case, that the convergence rate of the greedy algorithm using signed barycenters matches the one of the metric $N$-width defined with classical barycenters. We provide counterexamples showing that this fails for the other combinations.

papers.title: Finite propagation speed for evolutionary equations
papers.abstract: We study finite speed of propagation in the framework of evolutionary equations introduced by Rainer Picard in 2009. We establish sufficient conditions on the material law, which is represented by an analytic and bounded operator-valued function, and the unbounded spatial operator that ensure finite speed of propagation of information for solutions. Assuming a linear-in-frequency coercivity bound for spatially local material laws, we prove propagation on backward light cones for weighted $L_2$ solutions without a finite initial time, thus identifying hyperbolic-type evolutionary equations. The characteristic-speed threshold depends on the coercive coefficient and the principal spatial matrices, but not on bounded memory or delay terms or potential positive fractional temporal contributions. We illustrate the result with the scalar wave equation, Maxwell's equations, a fractional model in elasticity, and dual-phase-lag thermoelasticity.

papers.title: Optimal Polynomial Approximants vanishing arbitrarily close to the origin
papers.abstract: This work concerns a sequence of stable polynomials on the bidisk whose affine optimal polynomial approximants in the Hardy space of the bidisk have zero varieties that come arbitrarily close to the origin.

papers.title: Strong numerical radius orthogonality on bounded linear operators
papers.abstract: Orthogonality is an important tool for studying bounded linear operators. In this paper, we introduce the concept of strong numerical radius orthogonality of operators and then, discuss the properties about numerical radius orthogonality, strong numerical radius orthogonality of operators as well as relationship between them.

papers.title: Stable phase retrieval from operator measurements
papers.abstract: A known result of Cahill, Casazza and Daubechies [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B3(2016), 63-76] states that no frame in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space does stable phase retrieval. We show that stable recovery becomes possible for more general operator measurements, but only at a single exponent. Given a system of bounded operators $\{A_j\}_{j\in J}$ on a real or complex Hilbert space $H$, we study recovery of $f\in H$ up to a global phase from the quadratic measurements $\langle A_j f,f\rangle$ and from their phase preserving square roots. We consider $p$-Bessel systems ($2\leq p<\infty$) for which we measure the quadratic data in $\ell_{p/2}$ and the square root data in $\ell_p$. In infinite dimensions, we show that whenever $p\neq 4$, no $p$-Bessel system of operators does stable phase retrieval. In the case of $p=4$, we show that stability still fails on any system of semidefinite operators. Nevertheless, we construct a system of rank-one operators, not all self-adjoint, for which stable recovery is possible. We also show that stability can be achieved on a system of self-adjoint operators of rank-two. For both types of measurements, we show that the stability can be tested on orthogonal pairs. This reduction preserves the optimal constant for quadratic measurements and, when the operators are semidefinite, for their phase preserving square roots. We deduce that in finite dimensions, uniqueness of recovery implies its stability. Finally, we show that whenever only the moduli of the measurements are retained, both the orthogonal reduction and the implication from uniqueness to stability can fail, already in dimension two. We also give second moment measurements in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) as a motivation for the quadratic model.

papers.title: Isomorphic nonembeddings of Lorentz spaces under tensor products
papers.abstract: The Lorentz quasi-norm on $L_{p,q}(0,1)$ is \[ \|f\|_{p,q} =\left(\int_0^1 [t^{1/p}f^*(t)]^q\,\frac{dt}{t}\right)^{1/q}, \] where $f^*$ is the decreasing rearrangement of $|f|$. Motivated by the isomorphic classification of Lorentz spaces (KuryakovSukochev2015,HuangSukochev2021), we ask whether $\ell_{p,q}\not\hookrightarrow L_{p,q}(0,1)$ persists under projective tensoring with a common factor. For $1<p<\infty$, $1\le q<\infty$, and $p\ne q$, we obtain the following results. Nonzero finite-dimensional factors preserve the nonembedding, as do nonzero $\ell_1$-FDD factors when $q>1$. A single factor $U$ makes both tensor products isomorphic to $U$ throughout this range. For each pair with $q>1$, there are two nonisomorphic separable absorbers with the metric approximation property. For $1<q<p<2$, a scalar $L_1(\Omega,\mu)$ factor over a standard probability space yields an embedding exactly when the nonatomic part of $\mu$ has positive measure. For $1\le p<\infty$ and $0<q<1$, we construct common absorbers under $r$-projective tensoring after equivalent renorming.

papers.title: The distortion problem and orthogonality
papers.abstract: Schlumprecht [Israel J. Math. 76 (1991), 81--95] constructed an arbitrarily distortable Banach space. We further study distortion on this space under orthogonality constraints and obtain the following results. The exact distortion of his renormings is preserved in every infinite-dimensional subspace when the unit vectors satisfy both mutual Birkhoff--James and isosceles orthogonality for any finite family of equivalent norms. There are basic sequences of unit vectors satisfying both orthogonality conditions pairwise whose norms in the renormed space converge to the lower distortion endpoint. The proof combines finite-dimensional norm estimates with supporting functionals and the Borsuk--Ulam theorem. Further results concern finite and approximate Roberts conditions and an obstruction to simultaneous Pythagorean orthogonality for auxiliary norms.

papers.title: The Garnett--Jones distance theorem for rectangles
papers.abstract: For the family of all axis-parallel rectangles in $\mathbb R^d$, $d>1$, we characterize the distance of a real- or complex-valued function of rectangular bounded mean oscillation (little bmo) to $L^\infty$ by the reciprocal of its critical exponential integrability exponent. For each $\alpha>0$ at which the rectangular exponential moment of $f$ is finite, we construct a bounded correction so that the residual has mean absolute oscillation bounded by a dimension-dependent constant times $1/\alpha$ on every rectangle. The proof bounds products of coordinate maximal operators between two sets in terms of the supremum of their density product over common test rectangles. Selecting a longest interval along each path lets us remove repeated visits to a coordinate, so the density exponent is independent of the number of factors. The maximal-operator estimate holds with every positive density exponent below $1/6$ in two dimensions and below $1/24$ in three dimensions.

papers.title: Operative Representation of Quasi-Arithmetic Means, Complex Branch Structure, and Covariant Commutator Defects in Iterated Logarithmic Operation Hierarchies
papers.abstract: We investigate the bidirectional family of commutative binary operations $\mathrm{Op}_m^{(a)}[x,y] = f_a^{(-m)}(f_a^{(m)}(x) + f_a^{(m)}(y))$ ($m \in \mathbb{Z}$) generated by iterating the scaled logarithmic Cauchy isomorphism $f_a(z) = \frac{1}{a}\ln(z)$ ($a > 0$). Our analysis focuses on three structural properties of this hierarchy. First, we show that for all $m \ge -1$ the associated quasi-arithmetic Kolmogorov-Nagumo means $S_{\mathrm{Op}_m}(\mathbf{x})$ admit a closed two-stage operative representation $S_{\mathrm{Op}_m}(\mathbf{x}) = \mathrm{Op}_{m+1}^{(a)}[\mathrm{Op}_m^{(a)}[\mathbf{x}], N_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(n)]$ with normalization factor $N_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(n) = f_a^{(-m)}(1/n)$, and prove that this internal operative normalizability via a distributive adjacent level characterizes logarithmic generators among continuously conjugated group operations. Second, we show that for $m \le -2$ and $n \ge 2$ the normalization factor leaves the positive real domain $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, motivating the analytic continuation onto the Riemann surface of the logarithm; there, a fundamental dichotomy emerges between the internal branch-index invariance of $\mathrm{Op}_{-1}^{(a)}$ and the associativity defect $\omega(x,z)$ generated by $\mathrm{Op}_2^{(a)}$. Third, for arbitrary levels $m \in \mathbb{Z}$ and sample sizes $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we derive the general covariance pushforward theorem $\mathrm{Sp}_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) = f_a^{(-m)}(\mathrm{Cov}(f_a^{(m)}(\mathbf{x}), f_a^{(m)}(\mathbf{y})))$ governing the commutator defect between mean formation and the adjacent operation.

papers.title: Essential norms of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees
papers.abstract: We establish characterizations of the essential norms of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. As direct applications of our main results, we obtain compactness criteria for such composition operators.

papers.title: One exponential or two? Invertibility tests for Jordan epimorphisms
papers.abstract: How many exponential factors must one test to recognise a Jordan epimorphism? Let \(T\colon A\to B\) be a unital linear surjection between complex Banach algebras, with \(B\) semisimple. Using a spectral-isometry theorem of Aznay and Chabbabi, we show that it suffices for \(T\) to send every product of two exponentials to an invertible element to force $T$ to be Jordan. If only single exponentials are tested, \(T\) is a Jordan epimorphism if and only if its kernel is a two-sided ideal, or equivalently a left ideal. A resolvent estimate on a logarithmic spiral shows that a single exponential suffices when the source is a \(C^*\)-algebra or the group algebra \(\ell^1(G)\) of a discrete group. A separate argument, which does not use the spectral-isometry theorem, shows that a single exponential also suffices when the target is a \(C^*\)-algebra with a faithful family of tracial states.

papers.title: Freedom is all you need
papers.abstract: The functional calculus allows for the rigorous analysis of functions of matrices or even operators. The free functional calculus gives the natural class of functions over any category. We initiate the representation theory for taking a generic free functional calculus to the classical nc functional calculus going back to Taylor, Voiculescu and many others, with an eye towards learning of categories. The functional calculus on direct sum closed and locally similarity (i.e. change of coordinates) invariant domains inherits the niceties of complex analysis and large-scale parallel networks, such as automatic analyticity, free universal monodromy, which gives a hypothetical explanation for beneficial overfitting.

papers.title: Weighted sum commuting maps with the $(f,g)$-Aluthge transform
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ denote the algebra of all $n\times n$ complex matrices, where $n\geq2$, and let $\Delta_{f,g}$ be the $(f,g)$-Aluthge transform associated with nonnegative continuous functions $f,g$ on $[0,\infty)$ satisfying $f(t)g(t)=t$ for all $t\geq0$. In this paper, we characterize all surjective maps $\Phi:\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C}) \to\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfying\[\Phi(\Delta_{f,g}(\alpha A+\beta B))=\Delta_{f,g}(\alpha\Phi(A)+\beta\Phi(B))\]for all $A,B\in\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$, where $\alpha,\beta$ are fixed nonzero real numbers. Without assuming additivity or linearity, we prove that when $f$ is nonconstant, $\Phi$ must be of the form $\Phi(A)=cUAU^*$ or $\Phi(A)=cU\overline{A}U^*$ for all $A$, where $U$ is a fixed unitary matrix, $\overline{A}$ denotes the entrywise complex conjugate of $A$, and $c$ is a nonzero complex scalar. Moreover, we completely determine the possible values of $|c|$, which form either $\{1\}$, $q^{\mathbb{Z}}$ for some $q>1$, or $(0,\infty)$. When $f$ is constant, we show that $\Phi(A)=S(A)+D$ for all $A$, where $S$ is a surjective $\mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\beta)$-linear map and $D\in\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfies $(\alpha+\beta-1)D=0$.

papers.title: Rigidity in the Lichnerowicz inequality for word-length semigroups
papers.abstract: We give an operator-algebraic characterization of Cayley graphs that are partial cubes, that is, embed isometrically into a hypercube. More precisely, noncommutative versions of the Lichnerowicz inequality control the spectral gap of the generator of a quantum Markov semigroup by the constant in the complete $\Gamma_2$-criterion of Junge and Zeng or the constant in the geometric Ricci criterion of Junge, LaRacuente and Li. We show that for word-length semigroups on group von Neumann algebras, equality in either of these inequalities occurs exactly when the Cayley graph is a partial cube.

papers.title: On C*-nuclearity of graph operator systems
papers.abstract: We classify the set of finite simple undirected graphs whose corresponding graph operator system is C*-nuclear. We prove that the operator system associated to the graph is C*-nuclear if and only if the graph is 2-chordal, as defined by McCullough. In particular, we present the first known example of a non-chordal graph whose graph operator system is C*-nuclear, as well as the first known examples of graph operator systems which are not C*-nuclear.

papers.title: Martingale Transforms and Subsequence Estimates in Noncommutative \(L_p\)-Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a transference principle from martingale transform inequalities to subsequence estimates for weakly null sequences. As applications, for every von Neumann algebra $\M$, (1) we show that, every bounded sequence in the Haagerup space $L_1(\M)=\M_*$ has either a norm-convergent subsequence or a $2$-co-lacunary subsequence, answering an open problem of Parcet and Randrianantoanina; (2) we prove that every UMD Banach space has the uniform USP, which in particular yields uniform USP for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<\infty$, answering a question posed by Oikhberg and Spinu; (3) we answer an open problem of Haagerup, Rosenthal and Sukochev for the upper $\ell_p$ estimates for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<2$, in the affirmative; (4) we also answer the problem of whether every $2$-strictly singular operator on a noncommutative $L_1$-space is automatically Dunford--Pettis.

papers.title: Isomorphisms and representations of noncommutative function algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a noncommutative (NC) variety in a NC operator ball. We study the dual operator algebra $H^\infty(V)$ of bounded NC functions on $V$, and the operator algebra $A(V)$ obtained as the closure of NC polynomials in $H^\infty(V)$. We identify the space of weak-$*$ continuous finite-dimensional representations of $H^\infty(V)$ as the similarity envelope $\widetilde{V}$ of $V$, and equip $\widetilde{V}$ with a metric which turns $\widetilde{V}$ into a complete invariant for $H^\infty(V)$, in the sense that $H^\infty(V)$ is weak-$*$ continuously isomorphic to $H^\infty(W)$ if and only if $\widetilde{V}$ and $\widetilde{W}$ are NC biholomorphic via a bi-Lipschitz map. Similar results are obtained in the completely bounded category as well as for the algebras $A(V)$ when $V$ is assumed homogeneous. In the case of homogeneous varieties $V$ and $W$, we obtain a sharper classification result, by which $H^\infty(V)$ is (completely) boundedly isomorphic to $H^\infty(W)$ if and only if there is a linear map which gives a bi-Lipschitz bijection between $\widetilde{W}$ and $\widetilde{V}$. The reduction to the linear case in the generality we work in depends on showing that the existence of maps implies the existence of origin-fixing maps, which we show using a novel ``two-circle trick" of independent interest. In the important case where the varieties are the full NC operator balls we find a striking rigidity phenomenon: if $A(B_E)$ and $A(B_F)$ are completely boundedly isomorphic then $E$ and $F$ are completely isometric. We also present a variety of examples illustrating the results and their sharpness, showing how several results from the literature fail to generalize to the setting studied here.

papers.title: SVarM: Linear Support Varifold Machines for Classification and Regression on Geometric Data
papers.abstract: Despite progress in the rapidly developing field of geometric deep learning, performing statistical analysis on geometric data--where each observation is a shape such as a curve, graph, or surface--remains challenging due to the non-Euclidean nature of shape spaces, which are defined as equivalence classes under invariance groups. Building machine learning frameworks that incorporate such invariances, notably to shape parametrization, is often crucial to ensure generalizability of the trained models to new observations. This work proposes \textit{SVarM} to exploit varifold representations of shapes as measures and their duality with test functions $h:\mathbb{R}^n \times S^{n-1} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$. This method provides a general framework akin to linear support vector machines but operating instead over the infinite-dimensional space of varifolds. We develop classification and regression models on shape datasets by introducing a neural network-based representation of the trainable test function $h$. This approach demonstrates strong performance and robustness across various shape graph and surface datasets, achieving results comparable to state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters.

papers.title: Recovery guarantees for compressed sensing photoacoustic tomography
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic tomography is an emerging medical imaging technology whose primary aim is to map the high-contrast optical properties of biological tissues by leveraging high-resolution ultrasound measurements. Mathematically, this can be framed as an inverse source problem for the wave equation over a specific domain. In this work, for the first time, it is shown how, by assuming signal sparsity, it is possible to establish rigorous stable recovery guarantees when the data collection is given by spatial averages restricted to a sparse, randomly sampled portion of the boundary. Our framework encompasses many approaches that have been considered in the literature. The result is a consequence of a general framework for subsampled inverse problems developed in previous works and refined stability estimates for an inverse problem for the wave equation with surface measurements.

papers.title: Orlicz space relaxation of total variation denoising
papers.abstract: We consider variational image denoising with spatially dependent Orlicz regularization and introduce an Orlicz--Sobolev approximation of the ROF model based on a scaled $L\log L$-type density. For a general class of uniformly superlinear integrands satisfying a $\Delta_2$-condition, we establish existence and uniqueness of minimizers and derive a Fenchel dual problem with dual attainment and pointwise optimality conditions. We then specialize the framework to a logarithmic density whose correction is activated above a prescribed local gradient scale. For this model, we obtain explicit expressions of the Fenchel dual and optimality conditions as well as a pointwise radial formula for the dual proximal map involving the Lambert $W$-function. As the logarithmic parameter tends to zero, we prove equicoercivity and $\Gamma$-convergence to the ROF functional, together with convergence of the corresponding minimizers. Numerical illustrations indicate that the logarithmic correction can reduce staircasing for diffuse transitions, while retaining behavior comparable to ROF for sharp interfaces and a natural image.

papers.title: Harmonic mean closed vector lattices
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of the harmonic mean on certain Archimedean vector lattices, which we call harmonic mean closed. Using this concept, we provide a new characterization of positive orthogonally additive polynomials from a harmonic mean closed Archimedean vector lattice to a uniformly complete Archimedean vector lattice space entirely in terms of harmonic means. This result yields polynomial versions of the QM-AM-GM-HM inequalities on Archimedean vector lattices where the only additional requirement on the domain space is that it is harmonic mean closed.

papers.title: Monotonicity properties of Hadamard weighted geometric means of bounded sets of positive kernel operators
papers.abstract: We prove new monotonicity properties for joint and generalized spectral radius and their essential versions, operator norm, Hausdorff measure of non-compactness and numerical radius of products and sums of Hadamard weighted geometric means of positive kernel operators on appropriate Banach function spaces. Our results extend recent results on weighted geometric symmetrizations of bounded sets of such operators defined on $L^2$. To our knowledge, several proved properties in this generality are new even in the finite dimensional case and also in the case of singelton sets.

papers.title: Hardy operators: In the footsteps of Brown, Halmos, and Shields
papers.abstract: This paper discusses the two classical Hardy operators $\mathcal{H}_{1}$ on $L^2(0, 1)$ and $\mathcal{H}_{\infty}$ on $L^2(0, \infty)$ initially studied by Brown, Halmos and Shields. Particular emphasis is given to the construction of explicit cyclic and $*$-cyclic vectors in conjunction with a characterization of their invariant and reducing subspaces. We also provide a complete description of the frame vectors for $I - \mathcal{H}_{1}^{*}$.

papers.title: On some geometrization of compact metric spaces: A solution to the Banach-Ulam conjecture
papers.abstract: We propose a geometrization of compact metric spaces that is based on ideas of S. Banach and J. Mycielski. Then we prove the following conjecture of S. Banach and S. Ulam from 1935: in every compact metric space there exists a finitely additive probability measure, invariant under congruences. Moreover, our techniques allow us to solve a problem of M. Talagrand related to the Marczewski problem and the Banach-Tarski paradox with pieces having the property of Baire. We give also a very simple proof of the conjecture of Ulam about the product Lebesgue measure in the Hilbert cube and explain the existing results about congruence-invariant Borel measures in the language of our geometrization.

papers.title: On the dynamics of weighted shifts on Fr\'echet sequence spaces over trees
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give characterizations of Li--Yorke chaos, mean Li--Yorke chaos and distributional chaos for weighted backward shifts acting on general Fr\'echet sequence spaces over directed trees. As corollaries, we obtain explicit characterizations in the setting of K\"othe spaces $\lambda_p(A,V)$, where $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ and $V$ is a directed tree. In particular, we obtain criteria for the case of the classical Banach spaces $\ell^p(V)$, $p\in[1,\infty)$, and $c_0(V)$.

papers.title: Extensions from positive and full unit spheres of $C^\infty([0,1])$ with compatible Frechet metrics
papers.abstract: We study how the order of positivity determines the form of a linear isometric extension from the positive unit sphere of $C^\infty([0,1],\mathbb F)$, where $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$. At order zero, positivity means that $f(t)\in[0,\infty)$ for every $t\in[0,1]$. At order $m\ge1$, we require $f^{(m)}(t)\in[0,\infty)$ for every $t\in[0,1]$ and $f^{(j)}(x_0)\in[0,\infty)$ for $0\le j<m$, where $x_0$ is a fixed anchor. For the compatible Fr\'echet metrics $\rho_{m,p}$ studied here, we prove that every surjective isometry of the positive unit sphere extends uniquely to a surjective $\mathbb F$-linear isometry of the whole space. This holds for all $1\le p\le\infty$ at order zero and for $p=\infty$ under an explicit anchor condition at higher orders. At order zero, the extension either fixes every function or acts by reflection of the interval. Reflection is possible exactly when $p=\infty$ or $x_0=1/2$. At higher orders, the extension acts on the $m$th derivative by the identity or reflection and may permute the lower-order derivative values at the anchor. A counterexample shows that, for a different compatible metric, reflection can preserve distances on the positive unit sphere without admitting a real-linear isometric extension. We also classify the surjective isometries of the full unit sphere at order zero and prove that each extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the whole space.

papers.title: Commutants of diagonal operators
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is devoted to the profound and comprehensive characterization when diagonal operators having the minimal, tiny or double commutant property on a separable Hilbert space, in terms of the topological and geometric properties of their spectra.
